newsitem.title: ITALY: As lira ERM return nears, will BOI cut rates?.
newsitem.headline: As lira ERM return nears, will BOI cut rates?.

text.p: With the lira's return to the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) looking imminent, financial markets are in overdrive trying to guess whether the Bank of Italy will cut interest rates now or wait till later.

Some economists say an improving inflation outlook makes conditions ripe for a rate cut of 50 to 75 basis points as soon as Friday evening but others say the possibility of the lira's ERM return may make the Bank of Italy pause.

Preliminary November data from six sample Italian cities show a year on year inflation rate of 2.6 percent. Data from four more cities after markets close on Friday are expected to confirm that level or even show 2.5 percent, against October's 3.0 percent, economists say.
"We think this sets them up for a rate cut pretty soon," said Dominic Konstam, economist at Credit Suisse First Boston.
"They could even do it today after we get the confirmation. They have moved very quickly before after the CPI," he said.

A senior source at a banking congress in Frankfurt said Italy had requested a meeting of the European monetary committee be called for this Saturday, although a Commission spokesman said he could not confirm or deny the statement.
In the bond market, dealers said trade has stalled with players waiting for signs that a re-entry will definitely take place this weekend and what this means for interest rates.
Dealers said many expected a cut in the 7.5 percent discount rate after a lira re-entry, either by the end of November or later in December.
But Konstam argued returning with high interest rates and then cutting rates once the lira is back in the grid would run counter to the objective of having a stable currency.

"They have to cut rates once more before ERM re-entry," Konstam said in London. "The philosophy is it doesn't make sense to go into a fixed exchange rate system with rates still way above your counterparts' because it's a way of saying you haven't yet earned credibility while you were outside the system."
"You need to show your currency is stable with respect to a more convergent interest rate." he added.

Riccardo Barbieri, senior economist at Morgan Stanley in London, who did not rule out the inflation rate for November coming in at 2.5 percent, said a 50 basis point cut as early as Friday was possible.
In Italy, some economists said it was precisely because of the likely ERM return that the central bank would wait to ease.

Martino Dolfini, economist at Chase Manhattan in Milan, expected a cut of around 70 basis points by Christmas but said it would not make sense to cut rates immediately before or after a lira ERM return.
"With a return of the lira to the ERM the Bank of Italy does not want to give external shocks to the exchange rate," he said.

But with initial December CPI set for release mid-December and forecast under three percent, and approval of the 1997 budget package in the upper house of parliament, the scene would be set for an easing before the year end, he said.
Bruno Rovelli at Bank of America here expected a 50 basis point easing before the year end, once the budget, December inflation and contract negotiations with engineering workers were out of the way.
"This cut would counterbalance the fall in inflation and the strengthening of the lira in the ERM," Rovelli said.

Ken Wattret, economist at Paribas in London, said: "A post-ERM (re-entry) cut would be better received by the markets. A rushed cut would give the impression it was linked to ERM re-entry rather than the outlook for inflation."
